questions.q: According to this lesson, when should you reach for the Log Analytics data-query API instead of the Sentinel management REST API?
options: When you need to permanently delete a Sentinel workspace
When you need to analyze or aggregate raw log data using KQL, rather than act on a specific incident object
When you need to grant Azure AD admin consent
When you need to change which region a Sentinel workspace is deployed in
questions.explain: The Log Analytics data-query API runs KQL against raw tables like SecurityIncident for analysis; the management REST API is for acting on incident objects (listing, updating status/classification/owner).

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what does logs_client.query_workspace() return when response.status is LogsQueryStatus.SUCCESS?
options: A pre-formatted PDF report
An OAuth access token
A list of table objects, from which rows can be converted into dictionaries using the table's columns and rows
Nothing -- query_workspace only confirms the query is valid
questions.explain: response.tables[0] gives a table object; the lesson's code zips table.columns with each row in table.rows to build a list of dictionaries.

questions.q: Why does closing a Sentinel incident in this lesson require a separate requests.patch() call instead of using the LogsQueryClient?
options: Because incidents cannot be updated through any API, only through the portal
Because PATCH calls require a different programming language
Because LogsQueryClient only works with Defender XDR, not Sentinel
Because LogsQueryClient is read-only against log data and cannot update incident objects
questions.explain: azure-monitor-query's LogsQueryClient is for querying log data; updating an incident's status, classification, or owner requires calling the Sentinel management REST API directly.

questions.q: What determines which resource a token issued by the same ClientSecretCredential object can be used against?
options: The scope requested via credential.get_token(), e.g. "https://management.azure.com/.default" versus a different resource URI
The length of the client secret
The number of KQL queries already run that day
Whether the request uses HTTP or HTTPS
questions.explain: One azure-identity credential object can be reused across services; the resource scope passed to get_token() (or used internally by an SDK client) determines what the resulting token is valid for.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what Azure role is the minimum required to successfully PATCH a Sentinel incident's status and classification?
options: Global Administrator
Reader on the subscription only
No role is required if the client secret is valid
Sentinel Contributor on the workspace
questions.explain: Sentinel Reader is enough to run KQL and list incidents, but updating status, classification, or owner through a PATCH call requires Sentinel Contributor on the workspace.
